anomalies.observed: The two 120 Ω CAN termination parts are not connected across their respective CAN differential pairs. R81 pin 1 is on U2 CANL net /NET0020, but R81 pin 2 goes only to SW2 pin 1. R53 pin 1 is on U19 CANL net /NET0192, but R53 pin 2 goes only to SW2 pin 2. SW2 pins 3 and 4 are on the CANH nets /NET0067 and /NET0167. With SW2 being a SW_DIP_x02, its internal switches pair pins 1-2 and 3-4, so closing SW2 joins the two CANL nets together and the two CANH nets together rather than connecting each 120 Ω resistor from CANH to CANL.
anomalies.expected: A 120 Ω termination resistor should connect the corresponding CANH and CANL nodes (for example R81 between /NET0167 and /NET0020, and R53 between /NET0067 and /NET0192), or a proper multi-pole switch should connect each termination resistor to its own CANH node when enabled.
anomalies.impact: The CAN buses are not correctly terminated; if SW2 is closed, the two buses are bridged together instead of receiving proper per-bus termination. This can cause unreliable CAN communication or short the buses together.

anomalies.observed: Both isolated CAN transceivers have their primary ground and isolated bus ground tied to the same GND net: U2 pin 4 GND1 and U2 pin 5 GND2 are both on GND, and U19 pin 4 GND1 and U19 pin 5 GND2 are both on GND.
anomalies.expected: For an isolated CAN transceiver, the isolated-side ground (GND2) should be on a separate isolated ground net, not tied to the logic ground (GND1/GND), if the design intends isolated CAN buses.
anomalies.impact: The galvanic isolation barrier of the CAN transceivers is defeated, so the CAN buses are not isolated as intended and can introduce ground loops or lose the expected isolation protection.

anomalies.observed: The LTC4412 ideal-diode controller has VIN on USB VBUS net NET0183 and SENSE on the +5V rail, but the P-channel MOSFET Q7 is connected with its source on +5V and its drain on NET0183.
anomalies.expected: For an LTC4412 ideal-diode/OR-ing path from USB VBUS into the +5V rail, the P-FET source should be on the input side (NET0183) and the drain should be on the output/SENSE side (+5V), so the FET can conduct USB power into +5V while blocking reverse current.

evidence.quote: LTC4412 controller and p-ch mosfet. need reverse current protection mostly

anomalies.impact: USB VBUS cannot properly power the +5V rail through the ideal-diode circuit, and the board may back-feed the +5V rail into the USB connector instead of blocking reverse current.
